```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Tan AYF, Schneck K, Garhyan P, Chan ECY, Tham LS. Evaluation of
  Four Semi-Mechanistic Models for Predicting Glycemic Control With a Glucagon
  Receptor Antagonist in People With Type 2 Diabetes. CPT Pharmacometrics Syst
  Pharmacol. 2025;14:1381-1390.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70058> (open access; the final
  parameter estimates are in Supplementary Tables S2-S6).
* Model equations: the paper describes the structures in words and in its
  Figure 2 and states that each HbA1c model "largely retained" its original
  base structure. The equations used here are those of the original
  frameworks as deposited in NONMEM form by Kunina et al. (CPT
  Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol. 2022;11:1443-1457, supplements S2-S6,
  <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12854>), an earlier comparison of the same
  HbA1c models.

Adomeglivant (LY2409021) is an oral glucagon receptor antagonist; the paper
refers to it only by its development code. Tan 2025 first fit a population PK
model and then, sequentially on the individual PK estimates, four alternative
semi-mechanistic HbA1c models to a 4-week Phase 1b study, and judged each by
how well it predicted HbA1c after 24 weeks in a Phase 2b study. Each HbA1c
model is a separate file that carries the shared PK model:

```{r models}
mods <- c(
  ADOPT = "Tan_2025_adomeglivant_adopt",
  FFH = "Tan_2025_adomeglivant_ffh",
  FHH = "Tan_2025_adomeglivant_fhh",
  IGRH = "Tan_2025_adomeglivant_igrh"
)
for (m in names(mods)) {
  cat(m, ":", rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(mods[[m]]))$description, "\n\n")
}
```

| Model | Glucose driver | HbA1c structure | Extra inputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADOPT | 24-h average glucose (AG), indirect response | indirect response with input `KINH * (AG + beta)` | WT on AG0 |
| FFH | fasting glucose (FPG) and insulin (FSI), HOMA steady state | indirect response with input `KINH * FPG` | baseline FPG and FSI, placebo-arm indicator |
| FHH | FPG, indirect response | 4 + 4 RBC transit compartments, glycation `KGL * FPG^gamma` | sex (Hb production) |
| IGRH | AG, indirect response | 12 + 12 RBC transit compartments, glucose-dependent lifespan and precursor glycation | none |

In every model adomeglivant inhibits the zero-order glucose input with an Imax
function of plasma concentration (the paper's mechanism: reduced hepatic
glucose output), and a fractional placebo effect PLAC acts on the same input
from the start of treatment.

# Population

The models were built on the Phase 1b study (NCT01606397): 47 adults with
type 2 diabetes on diet and exercise alone or stable metformin, randomised 3:1
to adomeglivant 5, 30, 60 or 90 mg or placebo once daily for 28 days (Table 1:
mean age 53.6 years, 83.0% male, 46.8% White, mean weight 82.2 kg, mean BMI
28.5 kg/m^2, baseline HbA1c 8.00%, fasting glucose 8.64 mmol/L, average glucose
10.2 mmol/L, 68.1% on metformin). Predictions were evaluated against the
24-week Phase 2b study (NCT01241448): 254 patients randomised 1:1:1:1 to
placebo or 2.5, 10 or 20 mg once daily (mean age 55.1 years, 67.3% male,
90.9% White, mean weight 92.2 kg, baseline HbA1c 8.05%, fasting glucose
9.27 mmol/L).

The same information is available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Tan_2025_adomeglivant_fhh")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its supplementary table
row. The table below collects the values, and the equations' provenance.

| Quantity | ADOPT | FFH | FHH | IGRH | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KA (1/h), IIV | 0.385, 26.2% | same | same | same | Table S2 |
| CL/F (L/h, 70 kg), IIV | 0.283, 18.0% | same | same | same | Table S2 |
| V/F (L, 70 kg), IIV | 24.3, 12.4% | same | same | same | Table S2 |
| WT on CL/F, `exp(e * (WT - 70))` | 0.0116 | same | same | same | Table S2 footnote c |
| WT on V/F, `(WT/70)^e` | 0.956 | same | same | same | Table S2 footnote d |
| CL-V correlation | 0.778 | same | same | same | Table S2 |
| PK proportional error | 0.290 | same | same | same | Table S2 |
| Glucose baseline (mmol/L), IIV | AG0 9.62, 13.2% | from data (FPG) | FG0 8.72, 18.3% | AG0 10.1, 18.5% | Tables S3, S5, S6 |
| WT on AG0, `1 + e * (WT - 70)` | 0.00507 | - | - | - | Table S3 footnote c |
| KOUTG (1/h) | 0.429 | - | 5.10 | 0.164 | Tables S3, S5, S6 |
| PLAC (fraction), additive IIV | 0.122, 59.7% | 0.0556 fixed, 150% fixed | 0.055 fixed, 141% | 0.122, 39.3% | Tables S3-S6 |
| IMAX | 0.167 | 0.698 | 0.320 | 0.151 | Tables S3-S6 |
| IC50 (ug/L) | 1620 | 2210 | 1900 | 1450 | Tables S3-S6 |
| KINH (%/h per mmol/L) | 0.000706 | 0.000906 | - | - | Tables S3, S4 |
| KOUTH (1/h), IIV | 0.00118 | 0.000955, 5.07% | - | - | Tables S3, S4 |
| beta (mmol/L) | 3 fixed | - | - | - | Table S3 |
| baseline FPG on KOUTH, `1 + e * (FPG - 8.2)` | - | 0.0563 | - | - | Table S4 footnote e |
| Disease progression (logit/year): BCF placebo, BCF drug-added, IS | - | -0.2, -0.2, 0.1 (fixed) | - | - | Table S4 |
| KINHB (g/L/day) | - | - | male 1.21, female 1.12 | 1.2 fixed | Tables S5, S6 |
| KGL | - | - | 0.000224 /day/(mmol/L)^gamma | 6.76e-6 /day/(mg/dL) | Tables S5, S6 |
| RBC residence / lifespan (day), IIV | - | - | MRTE 120 fixed, 5.53% | LS 120 fixed | Tables S5, S6 |
| Glycation exponent, IIV | - | - | GAM 0.741, 4.17% | - | Table S5 |
| Precursor lifespan LSP (day), IIV | - | - | - | 7.12, 52.3% | Table S6 |
| AG exponent on lifespan | - | - | - | GAMMA 0.427 | Table S6 |
| Glucose / HbA1c / other proportional error | 0.111 / 0.0279 | 0.102 / 0.0315 / FSI 0.744 | 0.0964 / 0.0420 / Hb 0.0407 | 0.0804 / 0.0409 | Tables S3-S6 |
| PK structure | 1-compartment, first-order absorption | | | | Results, Figure 2a |
| HbA1c ODEs, initial conditions | Kunina 2022 S2 (Moller 2013) | Kunina 2022 S3/S4 (de Winter 2006) | Kunina 2022 S5 (Hamren 2008) | Kunina 2022 S6 (Lledo-Garcia 2013) | Methods, Figure 2b-e |

Log-normal IIVs are entered as `log(1 + CV^2)` and additive placebo IIVs as
`(CV * PLAC)^2`, the inverses of the CV definitions in the table footnotes.

# Virtual cohort

The Phase 2b data are not public. Following the paper's simulation design
(Phase 2b arms, covariates resembling the Phase 2b population, 24 weeks of
once-daily dosing), each model is simulated in a cohort of 150 virtual
patients per arm whose covariates are drawn from the Table 1 Phase 2b
summary statistics. Baseline fasting insulin is not reported; it is drawn
log-normally around 6.9 uU/mL, the value that gives the 40% baseline insulin
sensitivity quoted in the Results at the median baseline glucose of 8.2 mmol/L.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2025)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2025)
n_arm <- 150
arm_levels <- c("Placebo", "2.5 mg", "10 mg", "20 mg")
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(4 * n_arm),
  dose = rep(c(0, 2.5, 10, 20), each = n_arm)
) |>
  mutate(
    arm = ifelse(dose == 0, "Placebo", paste(dose, "mg")),
    WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n(), 92.2, 18.2), 55), 160),
    SEXF = rbinom(n(), 1, 1 - 0.673),
    FPG = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n(), 9.27, 2.40), 5.5), 16),
    INS_BL = exp(rnorm(n(), log(22.5 / (0.40 * 8.2)), 0.5)),
    # HOMA beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity must stay below 100%
    # for the logit disease-progression terms of the FFH model.
    INS_BL = pmin(pmax(INS_BL, 1.05 * 22.5 / FPG), 0.95 * 5 * (FPG - 3.5)),
    PLACEBO = as.integer(dose == 0)
  )

week <- 168
make_events <- function(cohort, obs_times) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    filter(dose > 0) |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, ii = 24, addl = 24 * 7 - 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, ii = 0, addl = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
pd_times <- c(0, seq(week, 24 * week, by = week))
pk_times <- sort(unique(c(pd_times, seq(0, 24, by = 0.5), seq(648, 672, by = 0.5))))
ev_pd <- make_events(cohort, pd_times)
ev_pk <- make_events(cohort, pk_times)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sims <- lapply(names(mods), function(m) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    readModelDb(mods[[m]]),
    events = if (m == "ADOPT") ev_pk else ev_pd,
    keep = c("arm"),
    useLinCmt = FALSE,
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  s$model <- m
  s
})
names(sims) <- names(mods)
hba1c <- bind_rows(lapply(sims, function(s) {
  s |>
    filter(time %in% pd_times) |>
    select(model, id, arm, time, Hba1c)
})) |>
  group_by(model, id) |>
  mutate(dHba1c = Hba1c - Hba1c[time == 0]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels))
```

# Replicate published results

## Table 2: mean change in HbA1c at Week 24

Tan 2025 Table 2 lists, for each model, the mean change from baseline HbA1c at
Week 24 predicted from 200 simulated studies of 65 patients per arm, next to
the observed Phase 2b means. The simulated cohort above reproduces the
model-predicted column of every model.

```{r table2}
tab2 <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~Observed, ~ADOPT, ~FFH, ~FHH, ~IGRH,
  "Placebo", -0.446, -0.742, -0.243, -0.311, -0.574,
  "2.5 mg", -0.566, -0.899, -0.669, -0.557, -0.705,
  "10 mg", -0.897, -1.16, -1.15, -0.984, -0.905,
  "20 mg", -0.928, -1.30, -1.51, -1.26, -1.02
) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(arm, Observed), names_to = "model", values_to = "published")

wk24 <- hba1c |>
  filter(time == 24 * week) |>
  group_by(model, arm) |>
  summarise(simulated = mean(dHba1c), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |>
  left_join(tab2, by = c("model", "arm")) |>
  mutate(difference = simulated - published)
stopifnot(nrow(wk24) == 16, !anyNA(wk24$published))

wk24 |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels)) |>
  arrange(model, arm) |>
  mutate(across(c(simulated, published, Observed, difference), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Model = model, Arm = arm,
    "Simulated mean dHbA1c (%)" = simulated,
    "Tan 2025 model mean dHbA1c (%)" = published,
    "Observed Phase 2b mean dHbA1c (%)" = Observed,
    "Simulated - published (%)" = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r table2-gate}
fit <- wk24 |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(rmsd = sqrt(mean(difference^2)), max_abs = max(abs(difference)))
knitr::kable(fit, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  # Each model reproduces its own Table 2 dose-response: a mis-transcribed
  # IMAX, IC50, KINH/KOUTH or RBC parameter shifts arm means by 0.2-1%.
  all(fit$rmsd < 0.15),
  all(fit$max_abs < 0.3)
)
```

The cohort means sit within a few hundredths of a percent of the published
model predictions, inside the Monte Carlo spread of a 150-per-arm cohort. The
paper's comparison with the observed Phase 2b means therefore carries over:
it found a significant over-prediction of the reduction in every arm for
ADOPT, at 10 and 20 mg for FFH, at 20 mg only for FHH and in no arm for IGRH.

## Figure S1: time course of the change in HbA1c

```{r figure-s1, fig.height = 6}
hba1c |>
  group_by(model, arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(dHba1c, 0.05), Q50 = median(dHba1c), Q95 = quantile(dHba1c, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / week, Q50, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(
    x = "Week", y = "Change from baseline HbA1c (%)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles; compare with Figure S1 of Tan 2025."
  )
```

```{r glucose, fig.height = 5}
glu <- bind_rows(

  sims$FFH |> filter(time %in% pd_times) |> transmute(model = "FFH (FPG)", id, arm, time, g = fpg),
  sims$FHH |> filter(time %in% pd_times) |> transmute(model = "FHH (FPG)", id, arm, time, g = glucose),

glu |>
  group_by(model, arm, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(g), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / week, med, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Median glucose (mmol/L)", colour = NULL)
```

# Deterministic checks

## Baseline HbA1c against the closed-form steady state

For a typical patient (70 kg male, baseline FPG 8.2 mmol/L, FSI 6.86 uU/mL)
each model's HbA1c at time zero must equal the steady state of its own
structure, computed here independently of the model code. For the transit
models, with glycation rate `g` and transit rate `k` per compartment, the
non-glycated amount in compartment `j` is `rho^(j-1)` times that in the first,
`rho = k / (k + g)`, and total hemoglobin is the production rate times the
residence time.

```{r baseline-check}
typ <- tibble(id = 1L, time = c(0, 24 * week), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L,
              WT = 70, SEXF = 0, FPG = 8.2, INS_BL = 22.5 / (0.40 * 8.2), PLACEBO = 1L)
bl_sim <- sapply(mods, function(nm) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(nm)), events = typ, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$Hba1c[1]
})

transit_hba1c <- function(n, ls_day, g_day, prec = 1) {
  k <- n / ls_day
  r <- k / (k + g_day)
  non <- prec / (k + g_day) * sum(r^(0:(n - 1)))
  100 * (1 - non / ls_day)
}
ag_igrh <- 10.1 * 18.016
bl_closed <- c(
  ADOPT = 0.000706 * (9.62 + 3) / 0.00118,
  FFH = 0.000906 * 8.2 / 0.000955,
  FHH = transit_hba1c(4, 120, 0.000224 * 8.72^0.741),
  IGRH = transit_hba1c(12, 120 * (ag_igrh / 149)^-0.427, 6.76e-6 * ag_igrh, exp(-6.76e-6 * ag_igrh * 7.12))
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(model = names(mods), simulated = bl_sim, closed_form = bl_closed), digits = 5, row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(abs(bl_sim / bl_closed - 1) < 1e-8))
```

## Steady state holds without treatment

With the placebo effect and the FFH disease progression switched off and no
drug, every model must stay at its baseline for 24 weeks; any error in the 8-
or 24-compartment initial conditions would show up as drift.

```{r steady-state}
hold <- sapply(names(mods), function(m) {
  mod0 <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(mods[[m]]))
  mod0 <- if (m == "FFH") {
    mod0 |> rxode2::ini(plac = 0, dp_bcf = 0, dp_bcf_drug = 0, dp_is = 0)
  } else {
    mod0 |> rxode2::ini(plac = 0)
  }
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod0, events = typ, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame")
  abs(s$Hba1c[2] / s$Hba1c[1] - 1)
})
hold
stopifnot(all(hold < 1e-6))
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA, so the PK check is internal: at steady state
(day 28, roughly 11 half-lives after the first dose) the AUC over a dosing
interval must equal dose / CL/F for every subject.

```{r pknca}
# rxSolve's keep= drops a column named `dose`, so it is joined back by id.
pk <- sims$ADOPT |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, dose), by = "id") |>
  filter(dose > 0, (time >= 0 & time <= 24) | (time >= 648 & time <= 672)) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm, dose, cl)
dose_rows <- pk |> distinct(id, arm, dose) |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 648))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pk, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_rows, dose ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 648), end = c(24, 672),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca)
```

```{r pknca-check}
ss <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", start == 648) |>
  left_join(pk |> distinct(id, dose, cl), by = "id") |>
  mutate(ratio = PPORRES / (1000 * dose / cl))
summary(ss$ratio)
stopifnot(
  nrow(ss) == 3 * n_arm,
  # Same drawn CL on both sides: only trapezoidal error on a 0.5-h grid remains.
  abs(median(ss$ratio) - 1) < 0.01,
  all(abs(ss$ratio - 1) < 0.03)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Equations from the original frameworks.** Tan 2025 gives no equations; it
  names the four frameworks, shows their compartment diagrams (Figure 2) and
  reports the final estimates (Tables S2-S6). The ODEs, initial conditions,
  HOMA constants (5 and 22.5, with 3.5 mmol/L as the glucose threshold) and
  the 149 mg/dL reference glucose of the IGRH lifespan come from the NONMEM
  implementations deposited by Kunina 2022 (supplements S2-S6), which share
  authors with the Lilly team behind Tan 2025.
* **How placebo and drug combine** is not stated. Both reduce the glucose
  input and are applied multiplicatively, `(1 - PLAC) * (1 - IMAX * C / (IC50 + C))`.
  The maintainers compared this with an additive form `1 - PLAC - Imax(C)`
  against Table 2: the multiplicative form reproduced the ADOPT predictions
  much more closely (root-mean-square difference over the four arms 0.025% vs
  0.074%) and the IGRH predictions somewhat more closely (0.028% vs 0.040%),
  the two forms were equivalent for FFH, and the additive form was slightly
  closer for FHH (0.033% vs 0.047%). One form is used for all four models
  since they share the authors' code base. Placebo starts at time zero for
  every patient.
* **IGRH precursor glycation is dynamic**, i.e. the fraction of hemoglobin
  glycated during the precursor lifespan, `exp(-KGL * AG * LSP)`, follows the
  current AG, as in the original Lledo-Garcia 2013 model and the Bosch 2025
  implementation in this package (`Bosch_2025_glp1ra_hba1c`). Freezing it at
  baseline, as in the Kunina 2022 code, under-predicts the Table 2 IGRH column
  by 0.09-0.20%.
* **IGRH lifespan exponent sign.** Table S6 reports GAMMA = 0.427 for the AG
  effect on RBC lifespan, which "decreased less than proportionally with
  higher AG"; it is coded as the exponent -0.427 of (AG / 149 mg/dL), so the
  lifespan is 120 days at 149 mg/dL. AG is converted from mmol/L with
  18.016 mg/dL per mmol/L.
* **FFH baselines are covariates.** Table S4 has no baseline glucose or
  insulin parameter, consistent with the text: baseline beta-cell function and
  insulin sensitivity are derived from each patient's observed baseline FPG
  (`FPG`) and fasting insulin (`INS_BL`, uU/mL) by HOMA. The disease-progression
  coefficients are added on the logit scale per year, the form in which a
  positive coefficient is the deterioration the Table S4 footnote describes
  and 0.1/year moves a 40% insulin sensitivity by about 2% per year, as the
  Results state. The additional beta-cell term applies to drug-treated
  patients (`PLACEBO = 0`). The placebo effect is switched on for `t > 0`, so
  the algebraic FPG and FSI equal their observed baselines at time zero.
* **Fasting serum glucose** was used by the authors in place of fasting plasma
  glucose; the models' fasting glucose output is that measurement.
* **Hemoglobin.** In FHH total hemoglobin (g/L) is an observed output. In IGRH
  it is computed (`hb`) but was not fitted; KINHB was fixed to the value whose
  simulated baseline Hb best matched the observed baselines.
* **Residual errors** are the proportional SDs of Tables S2-S6.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariates are drawn from the Phase 2b means and SDs of
  Table 1 rather than resampled from the individual data; baseline insulin is
  assumed (see above), and 150 patients per arm are simulated instead of 200
  studies of 65 per arm, so the comparison is against the published mean
  predictions only.
* **Not reproduced.** The bias and precision metrics (Figure 4, Table 3) and
  the observed-versus-predicted intervals (Figure 3) need the individual
  Phase 2b observations.
